content.text:
I'd tell my son that the page points to one answer. Open the account at "פסגות" and buy "ילין לפידות מחקה S&P 500 (4D)", number 5139282. Putting in 500 ₪ a month for 10 years, on top of the 10,000 ₪ the page started with, adds up to 70,000 ₪. The page says I would be left with "86,492 ₪" after fees and tax, in today's money. I'd still call him before I did anything.

**What I looked at:**
- **Screen 1:** The title "איפה ואיך הכי זול להשקיע במדד" and the S&P 500 button, already chosen. Then four boxes: 10,000 ₪ today, 500 ₪ a month, 10 years, and "7 %" a year. The page filled those in itself; I didn't type anything. Then the big numbers: "הפקדתם 70,000 ₪" and "86,492 ₪", marked "הזול".
- **Screen 2:** On the right, "פסגות". Its line says "מה החשבון גובה ב־10 שנים: 1,057 ₪". On the left, the fund ילין לפידות with "דמי ניהול 0%".
- **Screen 2, right side:** The list of banks. לאומי leaves 83,396 ₪ and takes 4,541 ₪. הפועלים leaves 81,471 ₪ and takes 6,576 ₪. My kind of bank takes several times more than פסגות. That's what I really came to find out.
- **Screens 3 and 4:** I only glanced. More funds, with red minus numbers like "−1,268 ₪" and "−4,492 ₪", and English names like iShares and Vanguard. I stopped there, tired. I didn't open screens 5 to 10.

**What I skipped:** The coloured bar at the top of screen 2 and its small legend. All the little coloured tags (צוברת, חשיפה לדולר, נאמן). The "לא בחישוב" folds.

**What I didn't understand:**
- "מדד": on the news it means the price index, so I wasn't sure what it means here.
- "S&P", "4D", "ETF", "UCITS", "IE00…": English letters I can't read.
- "צוברת", "מחלקת דיבידנד", "נאמן 0.02%", "דמי משמרת", "קרן מחקה", "קרן סל", "חשיפה לדולר", "סס גם על שינוי המטבע".
- "אם הדולר לא זז מול השקל": what if it does move?
- The "7 %": is that promised? The page never says I could lose.
- The dotted underlines under the numbers.

**What bothered me:**
- The whole page is dark, with small grey writing.
- Too many numbers, and red minus signs everywhere.
- The sliders.
- פסגות isn't my bank. I've heard the name, but I wouldn't move money there without my son.
